title: Do Board Gender Quotas Matter? Selection, Performance, and Stock Market Effects
eligible_reason: Replication check (data/replication_logs/mnsc.2021.4200.md): published ITT regressions include a second absorbing treatment dummy (phase-in 'limbo') and a time-varying election-year control; no controls-free version is reported. Excluded under PROTOCOL Section 2.
design_notes: Section 6.1: 'We build a dummy variable reform period which takes on value 1 in 2013 for firms that changed their board in 2013 ... In 2014 the variable takes on value 1 also for firms that changed their board in 2014, thus leaving in the control group firms that changed their board in 2015.' The authors first replace % women directors with this dummy (ITT/reduced form), then use it as an instrument (Eq. 3, IV with firm and year/month FE). Only the ITT-with-firm-FE rows of Table 5 qualify. Ineligible in the same table: OLS rows (continuous % women), ITT without firm FE (year FE only, no unit FE), IV rows (instrumental variables). Table 3 (board characteristics) uses an 'adjusted before-after' design with a 'second' and 'reform' period dummies on stacked 3-year windows for the 2007-2010-2013 and 2008-2011-2014 cohorts, board FE but no calendar-time FE and no contemporaneous untreated units: not a unit and calendar-time TWFE. Tables 6, 7, A5-A8 are market-model event studies of cumulative abnormal returns (cross-sectional regressions), not panel DiD. Appendix A1 repeats board-characteristic comparisons across the three election-year groups in 2013 (cross-section).
estimators_reported: TWFE reduced form (ITT) with firm FE (Table 5)
main_or_robustness: main for the firm-performance section (Part II); the ITT is a secondary step to the IV
screener_notes: Eligible via 8 Table 5 ITT-with-firm-FE columns. Caveats: (1) the text file is the April 2018 IZA discussion paper DP 11462 (candidates.csv link), not the published Management Science version, so table numbers, columns and estimates must be re-checked against the published paper and its package; (2) the authors' headline estimate is the IV, so none of the eligible specs is flagged preferred (column 8 is the reduced form of the abstract's volatility result, so marking it preferred would be defensible); (3) the regression sample runs 2010-2014 for the share of women (outcomes also 2015); whether firms electing in 2015 are coded treated in 2015 (making all firms eventually treated) is not stated; (4) clustering is not stated for Table 5; (5) the monthly treatment timing for column 8 is not described. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only. Data: hand-collected board data (CONSOB, company filings), Orbis-AIDA and Bankscope financials, Datastream Tobin's Q, Bloomberg prices; the licensed series may not be redistributable (data_access set to partial pending package inspection).
